utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will continue with the examination in chief of our witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I think yesterday you were still examining the witness. I don't remember whether you were through.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and I'm to continue this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We're about to enter our examination. Yesterday we covered quite a lot of ground, and now I should like to talk about the 17th of April, '93. Did you tell us clearly yesterday when the Muslims left towards the road from the house of Anto Papic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What time was that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was sometime in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic, did you see him in the morning?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, Drago Josipovic was in my house, and we went over to Anto Bralo's to have coffee together. Drago Josipovic spent the night in my house. In the morning, we were at my place. Then we went over to Anto Papic's house, had a coffee with him together. We stayed --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you mean Anto Papic or Anto Bralo?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Anto Bralo. I'm sorry, I apologise. We talked there, and Marija Papic asked my husband and Anto Bralo to go to her house and feed the livestock, and Drago went to his house to feed the poultry which Drago Josipovic had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Just one more question on the subject. Who went with the Muslims toward the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was Anto Papic who went with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he the only Croat?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We are still talking about the 17th of April, '93. Did Anto Papic come to your house at around noon or in the afternoon; on the 17th, that is? On the 17th of April, did Anto Papic come to see you or not?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do you mean morning or afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Any time of the day.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When he took away the Muslims, Anto Papic did come to my house. He asked me for some clothes, if I had any clothes for a small child, because Mirsad Osmancevic's wife had a small child and she didn't have enough clothes for the child, so that Anto Papic came to me because I also had a small child, to give him something, if I had any. He asked for milk. We had a cow, so he asked if I could give them some, if I could spare some, so I still gave it to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you give him all that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I gave him what I could for the baby, because my son is slightly older than Osmancevic's son, but I gave him what small sizes I had and I gave him some milk. But Anto Papic brought it back to me. He did not manage to give it to them. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that your husband practically lived in Novi Travnik and worked?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he doing something with his shares in Novi Travnik and do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. My husband was given the shares from the Novi Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know when -- was your husband mobilised?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: While he was in Santici?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My husband was mobilised on the 19th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Before that, was he ever mobilised before that and did he go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was like this: My husband was not mobilised, but he did go out to stand guard, mostly because he would be bored and in order to meet people in the area. He knew the people there very little, so as to get to know people a little better, he went out to stand guard, but very seldom. I mean village guards, village guards around our road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How do you explain that it says there that he's a member of the regular HVO force and that before he was mobilised on the 19th of April, '93, he is registered there prior to that date? What will you say about that? You told us he was mobilised on the 19th of April, 1993. Was that the first time?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So how is it that these documents say, when he was issued those shares, why does it say that he had been mobilised before that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When the war was over, couriers went around the village and were making a sort of a list, and we were told that they were doing it because of the shares, to know when people were mobilised so that that could be entered into that list. I asked that courier, on my own responsibility, to write a different date so that he could get better shares, because there were stories that one could buy building materials for those shares, and we were building our house. The courier did not promise anything, but he said that he would try to do something, and I do not know what date he put.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any other Defence counsel prepared to examine or cross-examine this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise. I completely forgot to show the aerial photographs to the witness. I had them prepared in advance, and I simply forgot about them. So may I please show them to witness? Will the usher please help me?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Please draw a circle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: If you don't mind, may I ask the registrar to first of all give us a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is D24/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovac, can you get your bearings on that map? Can you find your way around the map? You can turn it round if you think it will be easier for you.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I only ask if this here --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the other witness's microphone be switched on, please. Could we have the other microphone switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you try to find Musafer Puscul's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not -- this photograph is not quite clear to me, but I think that Musafer Puscul's house is over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you put a circle?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Usher, could you please offer her this copy here, it is clearer, I think, and then I believe she will be able to orient herself better.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I don't quite find my way about this one. This is Ogrjev, isn't it? This is Musafer Puscul's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you please make a circle?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you now make a circle around Asim and Ramiz's house. No, put an "A" next to Musafer Puscul's house.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now draw a circle around Nazif, Asim and Ramiz's house.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe it's these houses here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you please put small circles, and then mark them all together with a "B". Now will you please draw a line from Musafer Puscul's house to those houses up towards the road.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: And you want me to put an arrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, do put an arrow. Can you see from Musafer Puscul's house in the direction of those houses?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This area between Musafer's house and these houses is in the clearing, it is all clear, so that you can see. There are no trees, and you can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you can see?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Oh, yes, you have a full view.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you now find Fahrudin Ahmic's house and draw a circle around it? Just slowly.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Somewhere here (marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Anto Papic's?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Anto Papic is here (marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you please move it a little, because we can't see. Take care. Don't make a circle around Omazic, so think.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is Omazic's house, and this is Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, up there, put a "C" next to Fahrudin Ahmic's house, put a "C", and next to Anto Papic's, put a "D". Will you now draw a line from "C" to "D", in the direction of "D"?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, if you look from this house, could you see if a group of people or somebody moved down this way?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is all quite clear. It is where people grow vegetables.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And what about cereals?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, cereals too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the 16th/04, was there lush vegetation or not?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could one see?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: As your house is down farther away from Nikola Omazic's wood, or below it, could you put a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Do you mean my own house, or my father's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No, not your father's but my (sic) house, the house that you own.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't really quite find my way around this photograph, but I think this is my house (marks).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you then make a circle and put a "G" next to it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, will you tell us, from your house to Anto Papic's house, which are Muslim houses, and then you will put numbers to them. I shall repeat: From Anto Papic's house towards the road, can you tell us Muslim houses, either on the right or on the left side of the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I may, I should like to make a correction. This is not my house. This is my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well then, put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I do apologise. Now I've found my way around this. This is my house, and this is a "G", and this is a Muslim house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, will you please tell us -- cross this out and tell us which is a Muslim house, and put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a Muslim house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now put a circle, and put "1".

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: And the owner of this house is Zeno Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And the other one?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The second one is a (indiscernible) house. I put "2", isn't it? It is Cazim Ramic who is the owner of this house. Do you want other houses towards Anto Papic's?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are there any other Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not in the direction of Anto Papic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And in the direction of the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the direction of the road, there are. This is Osmancevic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Put a "3", then.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is Nail's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So put a "4". Give us the full name.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mirsad Osmanecvic, Nail Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, did any one of these houses burn down?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, not one of these houses burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was anyone injured or killed from these houses near Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From these Muslim houses, nobody was injured in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I mean the 16th of April, '93.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, on the 16th of April, nobody was wounded or killed. On the 17th of April, Cazim Ramic's house was put fire to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was that the only house that was put fire to?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In our area, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What about other houses today?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They're all intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So when you look from Anto Papic's house towards the road, who were people who were killed on the 16th of April, '93?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I look from the house, then next to the road it was only Fahrudin Ahmic and Musafer was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is his last name?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Puscul.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was anybody else killed apart from the two of them?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Next to the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, before the road. Before the road. Next to the road, only Musafer and Fahrudin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And nobody else?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is these houses next to the road in my area, and in all those other families --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I wasn't asking you anything about that, only Puscul and Fahrudin Ahmic. Did Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic stand guard there?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic were on duty here, along this road towards Anto Papic's house, because this is really the strict area of our village, and elsewhere were other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So between Drago Josipovic's house to Anto Papic's house, that is where they mounted guard?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I wonder if we can receive a copy of this particular aerial photograph which has been marked, because we have been using the big one, but of course, for the record, we need the small one, and also with a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So we can probably give the same number here. I mean, just discard this one and give the same number, so D24/4. Thank you. D24/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: They're identical. Mr. President, I should like to suggest at the same time that this aerial photograph, D24/4, be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I assume there is no objection from the Prosecution? It is admitted into evidence, yes. Thank you. I now turn to Counsel Pavkovic for the usual question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, other Defence counsel have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So we may now turn to the Prosecution. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good morning. My name is Franck Terrier. I am one of the counsel for the Prosecution, and I have a few questions for you. First of all, I should like to know whether yesterday afternoon or evening you spoke to anyone at all about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Not even with your husband?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. My husband wasn't well yesterday, and he spent most of the day sleeping, and I went for a walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In April 1993, your husband was working in Novi Travnik, and you were living in your father's house; that is, Nikola Omazic's house. Could you tell us how frequently your husband came back to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My husband never knew exactly when he would come home. He would come when he had a free day, and when he received his salary. He never knew when he would be free, because he was working in a company that worked on Sundays as well. So when he worked on a Sunday, then he would have a working day off, and he never knew which day that would be. He did his best to spend that day on the construction of our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it true to say that your husband was with his family on the 19th and 20th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My husband was at home then, because we went to Anto Bralo's, who spent a lot of time working on our house. My husband had a chainsaw, and his neighbour, Anto Bralo, asked him to come over and help him cut some wood. I think I that -- I remember that that is what they did on the 19th to the 20th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Similarly, on the 15th and 16th of April, 1993, your husband was in Ahmici with his family?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. On the 15th, we had a working campaign on the construction of our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In October and in April, did you consider the presence of your house to be a fortunate event for your family and for you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I don't really know what to say. This was a mere coincidence. We spent a lot of time working on our house. I didn't actually participate, but I prepared the activities because I was never sure when my husband would come, and I was in a hurry to finish the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, yesterday you mentioned Slavica Josipovic, and you said of her that at that time, referring to the period in 1993, that she was a very busy woman?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What do you know and what could you tell us about her political activities and commitments?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that Mrs. Slavica Josipovic was a member of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did Madam Slavica Josipovic talk to you or to your husband about her political engagements?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did Drago Josipovic talk to you about matters related to politics and the political commitments of his wife?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: After April 1993 --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that these questions are inappropriate regarding relations between husband and wife, that is, Drago and Slavica Josipovic, and it is inappropriate to ask the witness to comment on their conversations, because everything relates to individual responsibility in accordance with Article 7 of the Tribunal Statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but perhaps the Prosecutor is going to explain to us what is the relevance, in his opinion, of the questions he has just put.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the information of the Tribunal, I'm trying to set the grounds for these facts, and it is not without interest and it is quite relevant, in my view, to know the political, moral, philosophical context Drago Josipovic developed. The witness has told us, but it seems to me that a question deserves to be reviewed, especially since during her examination in chief, the witness mentioned Slavica Josipovic and referred to her important activities, implying that those important activities of Madam Josipovic had an effect and had consequences on the behaviour of Drago Josipovic, who had to do more of the home duties, if I understood well the testimony we heard yesterday. Therefore, I consider these questions to be quite pertinent. But of course the Judges will not place on the shoulders of Drago Josipovic anything that relates to his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, yesterday mention was made of Slavica Josipovic indeed, but rather about her work and not about her political engagements. So the Prosecutor has shifted from one area to another. It was stated that she was very busy because she worked in a private company both in the morning and in the afternoon, so no question was raised regarding her political activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: I consider that within the bounds indicated very clearly by the Prosecutor, the question is quite relevant. Of course, we need to understand the context, what was happening. Perhaps you could rephrase your question to limit its reach.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm going to go on to another series of questions, Mr. President, but if you wish me to rephrase my question, I can do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No, it's not necessary if you're going on anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, coming to the 16th of April, 1993, you told us that you and your husband were woken up by shots that you heard in the vicinity of your house. At that moment, you got up, you dressed, and you went towards Anto Bralo's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We went towards Anto Bralo's house because it was the house closest to ours and his house was made from stronger material than my father's and it was dug into the ground, and that was the reason why we went there. That is what I said yesterday, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Had it been envisaged in advance that in the case of any difficulties or conflicts, you should seek refuge in Anto Bralo's house? Was this conveyed to you by any authority; by the civil defence, perhaps, in advance?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The house that we took shelter in when the situation was tense due to Serb aggressors was that of Nail Ahmic. Nobody had designated Anto Papic's house as a shelter or anything like that, but we did so of our own accord. We went to Anto Bralo's house because we considered it to be safer than my father's, which was very old and there was no concrete slab and it was built some time ago from poorer material.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us how long it took you to reach that house and at what time you reached Anto Bralo's house? Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We got up as soon as we heard the fire. It took us perhaps two or three minutes to reach Anto Bralo's house, but we maybe spent some five minutes to get dressed and to get our three-year-old child ready and for us to decide where we would go. So perhaps we were in his house about twenty to 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that having arrived at Anto Bralo's house, you noticed Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you saw them, at what point in time?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't say that I saw them when I reached Anto Bralo's house, but I said that when I entered Finka and Anto Bralo's house, that we looked through the window and that we saw Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic near my father's house. That could have been about a quarter to 6.00, maybe a couple of minutes before that, and my husband and Anto Bralo stayed in front of the house and decided to go towards them, towards the road. We were watching all this through the window, and we saw that Anto Bralo and Franjo Kovac wanted to reach Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic, but Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic went towards the road and Anto and Franjo went towards the stable of Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You probably have already told us, but could you please repeat where Drago Josipovic was when you saw him on the 16th of April around quarter to 6.00 in the morning, according to what you have just told us? Where was Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic, where were they standing when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean at a quarter to 6.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic were moving along the road from Anto Papic's house to Nikola Omazic's house. They were closer to Nikola Omazic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: At that moment, was Drago Josipovic wearing the blouse of the uniform that you described yesterday, and was he carrying the weapon that you mentioned yesterday in your examination in chief?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I couldn't say that, because we were looking at that through Finka Bralo's window. Whether he was wearing this vest and carrying a rifle, I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But I'm not wrong, am I, that you said yesterday that Drago Josipovic on that day was carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you remember when you saw that weapon?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I personally met Drago Josipovic, and this must have been around 9.00 because we were, all of us, in between these two houses, Anto Bralo's and Nikola Omazic's, and Josipovic was wearing the vest and carrying the rifle. We were moving around, all of us, and we could see each other on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Are you certain regarding the weapon, because in the testimony given to us -- in the statement given to us by the Defence, it says that you were going to tell us that Drago Josipovic was without a weapon, and now today you're quite certain that he was carrying a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I said that he was without a weapon. That is only my note and the witness didn't sign anything, because at that time -- I won't go into it now, whether she saw the weapon or not through the window. What I considered important was the first moment when she saw him, whether he was wearing a weapon or not. The witness did not sign that statement, nor did I write down that Drago Josipovic was carrying a weapon in the morning at 5.00, after 5.00.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm saying also that I didn't say that Drago had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: The objection is rejected, and I should like to ask the Prosecutor to continue with the same line of questioning or any other questions that he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, on the 16th of April, 1993, at any time during the day, did you see or notice Drago Josipovic's family, and particularly his wife and his mother?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic's family I did see that morning; not his mother, but I did see his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you saw his wife? At what time on that day, the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw his wife in the morning in Anto Papic's house when she came to talk to refugees who were in Anto Papic's house, and she offered to help them, if necessary. I asked her where she was, and she told me that with her own car, mother-in-law and children, she had gone to Rovna because her parents were from Rovna, and that she had come to Anto Papic's house to offer those people her assistance, as far as that was possible. But I didn't see the mother that day. Drago Josipovic's mother is quite old and she could not walk alone, so her daughter-in-law transported her, together with the children, with her own car to Rovna, according to what she told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether at any point in time during that day, after a quarter to 6.00, the time when you saw Drago Josipovic, did Drago Josipovic have the opportunity or occasion to take care of his family? I'm thinking of his children and his mother.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the morning, about 5.30, there was very heavy shooting, and I believe that Drago Josipovic was thinking of his wife, children, and mother. As for whether he had an occasion to go home, I don't think so, because this was a clear space and there is no shelter. The path to his road from Anto Bralo's is exposed. These are all fields, and there's no shelter, so I don't think that Drago went towards his house, but I cannot guarantee that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You're telling us, madam, that when the shooting started at 5.30, Drago Josipovic was not in his own house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I didn't say that he wasn't in his house at 5.30. I didn't say that. I said that I saw Drago when I crossed over to Anto Papic's house, and I saw him through the window on the road towards Nikola Omazic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You went to Anto Papic's house, as you told us yesterday, to assist the Muslim refugees who were there, and we were told that 27 or 28 Muslims had found shelter in that house. You spoke --

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You spoke of Fatima, her husband, daughter-in-law, and grandchildren. Did you see any other Muslims heading towards Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did see Suhreta's family when she went over to Anto Papic's house, and I said yesterday that Jozo Livancic went to Anto Papic's house. I saw Mirsad Osmancevic with his wife and children going towards Anto Papic's house, but later I heard that Mirsad Osmancevic's wife did not stay in Anto Papic's house, but that she went to Rovna, to Jozo Cerkez's house, and that after some time, Drago Josipovic helped Mirsad to go to Rovna, that he gave him his vest, and after accommodating Mirsad in Jozo Cerkez's house, five or ten minutes later Mirsad called up Anto Bralo's house by phone -- I was present when he called -- and said that Franjo Kovac and Anto Bralo should come because Jozo Cerkez was under threat, because of Mirsad, as Mirsad was a member of the BH army before the conflict. My husband and Anto Bralo could not go and fetch him because at that moment they were not in Anto Bralo's house. When they tried to go there, he had already reached Anto Papic's house with his wife and children. I didn't see Zilka arrive, but I did see Zilka and Kijazim with their daughter-in-law and sons coming, but I saw them in the house. I think that is what I said yesterday, and that is what I stand by, and that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you explain, madam, the conditions under which the Muslim refugees were accommodated in Anto Papic's house? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can, because I know Anto Papic's house well. Anto Papic's house is small, old, with poor facilities. There are two rooms and a corridor that is being used as a kitchen to this day. He had two small children, a sister who is rather old, and a wife, who was not very healthy; she was sickly, and she died during the war. Twenty-seven or 28 refugees who were there virtually had no proper conditions for accommodation, because it is impossible to put up 30 people in two rooms and give them any kind of comfort. The house has no running water, no toilet, no bathroom. And Anto Papic himself, let me put it this way, was not very well off, and he was short of food for himself, and never mind for so many people. He just couldn't look after them. It was very difficult for him to look after them even for 24 hours because of those conditions and because of the conditions in his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yourself, madam, together with your son, found shelter in Anto Bralo's house. How many refugees were gathered in that house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Anto Bralo's house, the Croatian inhabitants were coming, the Croatian refugees. I was the first, with my son. I was followed by Marija Papic and Ljubica Milicevic, with her daughter, and then came Serafina Vidovic with her husband, we call her Finka Vidovic, and her husband. Then there was Jozo Santic, an elderly man from our area. And I think no one else. I think no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could it be said that the conditions in Anto Bralo's house were much better than those in Anto Papic's house, the Croats on the one hand and Muslims on the other?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, the conditions in Anto Bralo's house are better. Anto Bralo's house had a bathroom. Yes, the conditions were better, but nowhere were conditions such as to be able to accommodate three or four, never mind ten people. None of us had the facilities to take in ten guests at the same time, because as the host, you wish to extend hospitality to those people, in a sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Perhaps, also, it was not possible to disperse the refugees. On the contrary, it was necessary to gather them together. Was that your view?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say is that if all those refugees were gathered in the condition that you have described in Anto Papic's house, and not spread out in other houses, like Anto Bralo's, maybe it was decided that those refugees should not be dispersed, that they should remain in a group.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that the refugees from Anto Papic's house moved freely and came to Anto Bralo's house, but they wanted to be together. Fatima came to Anto Bralo's with her husband. Zilka came with her husband. No member of Anto Bralo's family would have sent them back. We would have taken them in just like Anto Papic had done, but they wanted to be together. I personally think it was easier for them to be together, and they liked to be together. That is my view, my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: It is your opinion that I should like to hear. Was it possible for those refugees to leave Anto Papic's house, to cross the Lasva River on the Radak Bridge and to seek shelter somewhere on the opposite bank, on the side of Rovna? Would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean could those refugees go towards Rovna? Those refugees could go towards Rovna. Mirsad Osmancevic did cross Radak's Bridge. I told you that he went to Rovna, to Jozo Cerkez's house. Then there was a threat to that house, and then he came back across that same bridge, because that is the only link to the village of Rovna. They could have, but they moved freely, wherever anyone wanted to go. And Rovna, too, is a Croatian-majority village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, you said that they could have, but yesterday you told us that Mirsad Osmancevic, in order to cross the bridge, needed a camouflage vest, which he was lent by Drago Josipovic. So when you say that it was possible, one has an ambiguous impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should like to object to this question because the witness didn't say a protective vest; she said a camouflage vest.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mirsad did not ask for this vest, but Drago gave it to him so that he shouldn't be mistreated or provoked, because there were people, unknown people, who might recognise Mirsad as a Muslim, but wearing a vest, he would be safer. But it is not true to say that he could not stay in Jozo Cerkez's house. They received very well Mirsad Osmancevic's wife and children, but someone, one of the soldiers, threatened Jozo Cerkez that they would blow up his house because he was taking in Mirsad and Mirsad was a member of the BH army and war was being waged against the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, madam, how much time you spent in Anto Bralo's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was in Anto Bralo's house throughout that day, but I went to my own house very frequently. The distance between my house, Anto Bralo's, and Anto Papic's is very small. They are three houses that are closest to one another. I would cross into my house frequently. I had two cows, chickens, and other livestock. I needed clothes for my three-year-old child. So I would cross over to my house frequently, and if my neighbour, Finka, didn't have something, I would go to my own house to get it. I spent most of the time at Anto Bralo's house. Towards the evening we talked where we would go, where we would spend the night, and I said that I would go to spend the night with my child in my own house because my child was most comfortable in his own cot. I wouldn't sleep. I would watch out for the safety of my children. Then my husband said that he would also come to the house, and then Dubranka Santic decided to spend the night with us, and then we asked Drago Josipovic to come over and keep my husband company in case that we women fell asleep. So we spent the night in my house; that is, in Nikola Omazic's house. The other Croatian refugees stayed on in Anto Bralo's house. We did not sleep that night, but we just relaxed, but were watchful. We had to be ready at any moment in case firing should erupt again because the children were with us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: During the days that followed, the 17th, the 18th, and the weeks that followed, did you stay in that house, your father's house, Nikola Omazic's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 17th, in the morning, we went to Anto Bralo's. I spent all the night in my own house, but during the day I spent more time in Anto Bralo's house than in my own. I went to my own house only when I had to, but I spent all the nights in my own house. When my husband was mobilised on the 19th, I didn't dare sleep alone in the house. Then Drago Josipovic's mother came to my house on the 19th of April, and she stayed with me for a long time. Jozo Santic, too, when my husband was mobilised, then Jozo Santic came to spend the night at my place, and Simo Vidovic stayed at Finka's, so that we would each have an elderly man with us to provide some kind of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, madam, how many people who lived in your area were killed on the 16th or the 17th of April? Do you have any idea of that?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said along the road where we lived from the road to Anto Papic's house, Fahran and Puscul, Musafer Puscul, were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: If you don't know, you don't know. I'm not asking you the names. I just want you to tell us whether you know how many people were killed in that area.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Two. In my area, from the road where Suhreta Puscul is to the house of Anto Papic, two persons were killed. And there are other areas which I didn't comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You don't know? A last question for you, madam. You told us a moment ago that your husband kept guard duty when he came to Ahmici in April 1993. Could you be more specific and tell us with what weapon he kept guard duty?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't say that my husband went to Ahmici. My husband went to Santici. When he had a day off, he would come to Santici, not to Ahmici. My husband went to keep guard duty, to spend his free time in that way, and to associate with Bralo and Josipovic and Anto Papic. Sometimes he had a wooden toy rifle with him, which our children used to play with, because he didn't have a rifle. So he would carry the children's toy rifle with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have only two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that Slavica Josipovic and her children went to Rovna in her car, as I heard?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't see her going, but I heard that Slavica had gone by car with her children to Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you hear when that was?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Slavica told me when we met in Anto Papic's house -- it's very hard for me to say all these names -- that she was awakened by gunfire and that she fled in her car with her children to Rovna. She also told me that her house had been damaged and that she had seen, as she was leaving for Rovna, that the window had been shattered and that the facade and roof were damaged. She fled to Rovna in her car because it was impossible to go on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that Mirsad Osmancevic went to Rovna and so did his family?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could any of the Muslims in Anto Papic's house have gone to Rovna?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Any Muslim, if he wanted to, if he knew someone in Rovna, could have gone. Mirsad decided to go because he and the children of Jozo Cerkez had very close relations, so he decided to go to Jozo Cerkez's house because they were on very close terms. The other Muslims who were staying in Anto Papic's house could have gone to Rovna if they had known that they would find someone there who would take them in, but they were not so familiar with Rovna as they were with Anto Papic's house, so of course they felt more comfortable in Anto Papic's house because they knew him. When there was gunfire, nobody was worried about the conditions they would have to live in. The aim was to survive and whether you would be able to lie down and sleep or whether you would have to stand was not important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: One more question. The Prosecutor asked you if any Muslims had been killed in your neighbourhood, and you answered, "Two." However, this is a broad question. Can you tell us whether any of your Muslim neighbours were killed in the vicinity of your house or, rather, between Anto Papic's house and your house, and where were these people killed and were they your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had our own path leading from Drago Josipovic's house to Anto Papic's house, and on that lane, on the left and right side, no one was killed. But there is also another lane which leads toward a third road, and Fahran Ahmic and Musafer were killed on this other way. But on the lane leading to my house and Drago Josipovic and Anto Bralo's house, no one was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You say that none of your neighbours were killed and that these two were killed. Can you tell us how far the houses are from the road?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Their houses are close to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How many metres?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, Fahran's house is five to ten metres, and Musafer's is some 15 to 20 metres away from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me to be a bit more.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVAC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Musafer's house is close to their house, and Fahran's and his mother's house -- well, in my opinion it's close to the road. I never measured it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We don't have any questions for the witness. Mrs. Kovac, thank you so much for testifying in court. You may now be released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, may I ask you, who is going to be your next witness, Mr. Pranjkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Ivo Pranjkovic. I believe that this will be very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Pranjkovic. So it's misspelled, yes. So his name has been misspelled in the list. Ivo Pranjkovic. You are not seeking any protective measures, I gather.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone was not switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pranjkovic. Will you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I wish to greet the Honourable Court and all those present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning. Could you please sit down, and I will call upon Counsel Susak to start with the examination in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Pranjkovic.

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Good day to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you please introduce yourself to the Court? Would you tell us your first name, your last name, your birth date, where you live, and where you work?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Ivo Pranjkovic. I was born on the 30th of December, 1937, and I work in the Vitezit company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were you a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the reserve.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you were in the reserve?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We will proceed to ask specific questions. Did you go to the front line facing the Serbs or the Muslims during the war?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: During the war, I was mostly in the village guard and at a position which was called Kuber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you tell us what Kuber is?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was said to be a strategic point, a place where the borders of three municipalities meet, Zenica, Busovaca and Vitez, where there is a plateau the size of a soccer field which was supposed to be guarded against Serbian forces who could have landed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How many times did you go to Kuber?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where were you on the 15th and 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: At Kuber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you were at Kuber?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When did you go there?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And the year?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was 1993, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So on the 13th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know who else was there?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Before you tell us who was there, could you tell us what your position was there, who your commander was?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was the deputy commander in the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who was there in that group? Can you tell us the persons' names?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of April, we went there, and the commander was Zeljo Livancic. There was Mirko Livancic, Mirko Vidovic, Andjelko Vidovic, Anto Santic, Vlado Santic, Stipo Grgic, Stipica Grgic, Ivo Pranjkovic, Ivica Badrov, Ivica Safradin, Anto Buha, Zarko Kristo, Andjelko Vidovic, Jakov Opacak, and Ivica Plavcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So how many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Fifteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Kuber?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: We stayed until the day we were attacked and had to withdraw from the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How did you go to Kuber?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were sent there by the office for defence, since we were not sent to some faraway warfield, since we were in the village and the local patrol. So when we had time, the defence office sent us to Kuber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were you on a list, or how did they know about you? How did they know where you were?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were couriers in the village who knew and who contacted -- the late Nenad Santic cooperated with the office for defence and the authorities, so they knew when someone was free, and then they would send us to Kuber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they would give them your details and you would be sent there?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mentioned the authorities. What authorities were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was referring to the municipality authorities and the office for defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who was at the head of the municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: It was Ivica Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who was in the office for defence of the Santici municipality?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think his name was Stipo Zigonja

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Marijan?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Marijan Skopljak, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What was he?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was the president of the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You may have got the names mixed up. So Pero Skopljak was the president of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Marijan was in the government, but to tell you the truth, I don't know exactly what his function -- what his post was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, was there any civil defence in the villages?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the civil defence existed from before, and they were organised in some way and they performed certain duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was there a municipal Territorial Defence headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that the civil defence had been set up. Did anyone from the civil defence patrol the village?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from time to time when they were free.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the basis of what were these patrols held? Did they agree among themselves or how was it done?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the civil defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the same way as we did. When they had time and when they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So was it a thing that you discussed and agreed on?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because the village had to be defended against burglaries, looting, and such things that were going on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you were a member of the reserve HVO. Did you know that the military or civilian authorities confiscated weapons from certain persons in the area of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware of this because I didn't move around very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard something about some isolated cases, but I can't comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When you were in Kuber, you mentioned Zeljo Livancic?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that he left when you did, that he went to Kuber on the 13th of April?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and he was the commander of the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And you, what were you?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether he survived or not?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Zeljo was killed on the 17th of April, when we were attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: In the evening. It was between 18.00 and 18.30. I'm not sure exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was Josko killed as well?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and Stipo Grgic and Niko Livancic were also killed, and their bodies have never been found or buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they were declared missing?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know the village of Santici?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because I was born there and I still live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know or have you heard about D.D. Vitez? What is that?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: It's a building construction company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do they have a warehouse in Santici?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, they did then. Now it's privately owned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to ask the usher to take these aerial photographs, and then I will conclude my questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please show where the Ogrjev warehouse is belonging to the Vjeternica company which we just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be D25/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Pranjkovic, I have a larger photograph. It may be easier for you.

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you can compare the big and the small photograph and then mark the small one, but it's easier to find your way on the big one.

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: This is the main road (indicating), and I think this is the building (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you circle it, please, on the other photograph, on the small one? This is just to help you recognise what is on the small photograph.

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now circle Ogrjev.

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mark it with the letter "A".

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us where the road leads to the right and to the left? This is the main road?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it's the same road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So if you were to take that road, where would you be going, where would you arrive?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: To Sarajevo and to Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So to the right, could you tell us where the road leads?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the main road?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Does it go to Novi Travnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: If I was looking ahead, it would go to Travnik, and in the opposite direction, it would go to Sarajevo or Busovaca. Well, first Busovaca and then Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. So Busovaca and Novi Travnik. Now we are at Ogrjev. Do you know whether there is a fence around Ogrjev?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What kind of fence it is?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there are some concrete posts and wire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us whose houses are to the left or west of Ogrjev and whose houses are to the east?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: To the east, since I know the place, the house of Ismail Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you circle it, please, and mark it with "1"?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies) Left of Ogrjev.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now look at the Ogrjev fence. So where is Ogrjev?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: It's here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Whose house is to the left?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: To the left? To the left is the house of Murad Djidic, number 1, Sefika Pezer, Josip Vidovic. That's to the left or to the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please look at me, please? So Ogrjev is over there. Do you know where Ismail Ahmic's house is?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: To the east?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: To the east, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Of what?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Of the Ogrjev building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Whose house is on that side?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Mujo Ahmic and Mustafa Ahmic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you circle those houses, please, and mark them "1", "2", and "3"? Where is Ogrjev?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they are next to the Ogrjev fence (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You are indicating houses across the road?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't find this photograph completely clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, but I'm wondering whether it is really so crucial for us to have all the markings, because we know all these places. We have dozens of aerial photographs, and also we have a very good map produced by the Prosecution with all the houses and the names and so on. Is it so important? Also the witnesses can't get their bearings, and I can understand why, because it's so difficult. As I say, for the purposes of our proceedings, I wonder whether it is very important for us now to ask each witness to locate a particular house. I can the understand the question of the factory and the fence. Of course, we all know it is important for you. But I mean why don't we concentrate on this particular matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I will respect your decision, so I will only ask the witness to enumerate the houses on the left side of Ogrjev and on the right side of Ogrjev.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Don't look at the photograph any more. Just tell us Mr. Pranjkovic, just tell us whose houses are to the east of the Ogrjev warehouse?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: They are Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are they Muslim houses or Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: They are Muslim houses on the east. The nearest are three houses; Ismail Ahmic, Mustafa Ahmic and Mujo Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And to the west?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: To the west, Murad Djidic, Ado Becirevic, Josip Vidovic, Sefik Pezer and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We have finished with this area. As for Zeljo Livancic, some say that on the 16th of April, he was in Ahmici and in Santici. What do you say to that? Could he have been in Ahmici, considering what you said?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I say that he was on Kuber with us and that he couldn't have been there. He was with me and he was killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So do you think it's true, or not?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, whoever said that was not telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, the other Defence counsel have no questions, but I have only one comment: The witness listed the persons who were on Kuber with him. I think he enumerated 15. But the names of Zarko Kristo and Andjelko Vidovic are not in the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: You heard these two names? All right. So we will put the record straight and make the necessary corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel Pavkovic. I think, before we hear the Prosecution, we can adjourn now for half an hour. So we will reconvene at five to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Before I turn to the Prosecution, let me tell you that on Friday we've got to stop at 1.00 sharp, so we therefore wonder whether we could try to make an effort to get through with all the witnesses by Friday at 1.00, the list, to go through your list of witnesses. I, of course, am in particular making an appeal to Counsel Susak. If need be, we could start on Friday at 8.30, if we see that we need some more time, 8.30. So this is just an appeal to both parties to try to get through with the list of witnesses by the end of this week. You know why, because you know very well that we will skip one week, and that means that if some witnesses cannot be called to court, then they will have to stay here for a week or go back to their country and come back here. So it's time-consuming, expensive, and also bad for the witnesses. All right, so let's make an effort. Mr. Blaxill? Counsel Susak, did you want to say anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do hope that I shall be up to the plan and we shall conclude with examination of our witnesses as you just indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Pranjkovic, good morning to you, sir. My name is Michael Blaxill. I'm one of the prosecutors in this case, and I would like to ask you just a few questions, sir, as a result of what you said here today. Firstly, may I ask, where were you living in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: In Santici, the municipality of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Would Mr. Nenad Santic therefore have been a neighbour of yours at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You have stated that you were in the -- what became, at least, the HVO reserve forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When you were called to go to duty on Kuber, how did you receive your instructions?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I received the instructions from the office for national defence. There was a summons, and I had to join the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Would that be a summons by a visit from an official, or would that be communicated perhaps by telephone or some other form?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I received it in writing, as a summons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When you served on Kuber, did you do so in the same unit on each occasion?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When you reported for duty on Kuber, did all of you from the unit serve at the same time, or did the individuals rotate the duty at different times?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: We all performed our duty equally. We went when we were free, depending on how free one was, and then he would be called up and asked to take up his post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: How long would each person generally serve when they went to the lines at Kuber?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: From seven to ten days. Those were the shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So if I've understood you correctly, sir, you would have individual rotation in the unit, so one man might be serving seven days, his comrade would arrive, then he would finish and leave, then another comrade would arrive, and so forth; yes?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When you reported for duty on the 13th of April, 1993, did you in fact go to the lines with Mr. Zeljo Livancic?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: What arrangements did you have during the night up on Kuber? How did you arrange to stand guard and/or rest your troops?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Some people would be on duty for two hours, and then we would take shifts, and it went on like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Would it be correct that as the deputy commander, would you take sort of one shift and be with the men, and perhaps Mr. Livancic would take the other shift while you rested? Did you share your command duties that way?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, more or less. As I was the deputy, I was the one who took people -- who headed people on shift more frequently, more often. Later Zjeljo was in that building, or rather in that shed that we used, but at times he was the one who headed the shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So if you were heading the shift, you would actually be in the trenches, in the front-line trenches with the men; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: It is. Yes, I would take men to those points.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And the shed that was used, about how far from the trenches was that shed?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: About 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Was the shed visible from the trenches?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, because it was in the wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Can you recall, sir, what time was the last time you saw Mr. Livancic on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: He was with us all the time, so I just don't know. How can I define the time? We were together. We were together in that shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But do you recall any time, say, on the evening of the 15th, when perhaps you might have been in the trenches and Mr. Livancic had a period of time back in the shed?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Usually, being one of the older members of the group, I would merely take the shift to their posts and come back to the shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But do you recall, what about sleeping arrangements during the night? Do you recall whether you or Mr. Livancic took any sleep?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was the two of us who were on duty in that shed from the beginning of the night to midnight and then from midnight onward. So the two of us took shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: If you were on such duty and you were taking shifts, where would the person who was going to sleep, where would they sleep?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: In the shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: At what time did your shift end on the morning of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: At 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: At that time, do you recall where both you and Mr. Livancic were at 06.00 that morning?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I was on duty, and Livancic was asleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: By "on duty," do you recall where you were? Did you go out to inspect the men, or were you in the shed?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: During that shift, from midnight to dawn, or rather until daybreak, I would go once, but it was 300 metres. It's very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: How long would you spend out at the trenches with the men?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: As a rule, the commander or his deputy going to inspect the guards, he would stay there 15 or 20 minutes, perhaps, to see if there is anything new, if they need anything, and then goes back to the shed. Because until that time there were no problems at all, and there was no need for us who headed those shifts to be with men in the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: A little earlier, sir, you did say that there were periods of time when indeed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Blaxill, I understand there is no translation into French.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier says he has no problem, so I'm just wondering if it's individual equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier, could you follow it in French, and could you also hear the witness speaking French, I mean, because it seems that the court reporter cannot follow. All right. I understand we may continue now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Could you tell me, please, sir, when did you start performing your duties in Kuber? When was the first time that you were sent up to those lines?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date, but we began to go out to Kuber, well, a long time before the outbreak of the conflict, because we were guarding this plateau, this highland which could have been a very good place for the Serb assault or things of that kind. But I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Can you give me just a rough indication? Was it in 1992, was it in 1993, was it in the summer, the winter?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, in 1992 it was, but I cannot be more accurate as to the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you acquainted with Mr. -- well, you are acquainted, I believe, with Mr. Drago Josipovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether he was ever called to perform such duties up on Kuber prior to April 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't, as far as I know, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you acquainted with Mr. Zoran Kupreskic or Mr. Mirjan Kupreskic?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether either of them were ever called upon to do this kind of reservist duty on Kuber prior to April 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you acquainted with Mr. Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you aware as to whether he ever performed such duties prior to April 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: How long, sir, did it take to go from Kuber down to your home village of Santici on foot?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: An hour and 40 minutes or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You referred to Mr. Nenad Santic as somebody dealing with coordination of certain activities. Would it be true to say that Mr. Nenad Santic was a form of local HVO commander in the Santici region? Would that be a fair description?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Nenad Santic cooperated with the municipal government and with the national defence office, so he was a kind of associate. He cooperated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did your unit ever have direct contacts with Mr. Santic?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, really. As far as I do understand you, Mr. Nenad Santic transmitted -- he was the one who conveyed the orders or agreements regarding the guard duty, going to Kuber, and things of that kind.
