utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: But how would that actually be communicated? Would somebody meet with Mr. Santic down in the village? Would he come up to Kuber? How would that communication take place?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was usually couriers who did that. They would bring summons, instructions, and things of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you have any kind of radio communications with you on Kuber, as a unit?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Later on, sometime -- right before the conflict, we had a radio station which was out of work so we could not use it, but we had nothing in the beginning and it simply did not work properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Well, in about April of 1993, did you have any kind of walkie-talkie radios or Motorolas or anything to assist your communications?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I told you already, at that time precisely we did have a kind of a station, but it wasn't really in good working order and we had no walkie-talkies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Did you ever have radio communications with anyone in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Are you aware of any radio installations in Ahmici at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Just one final question, sir. During the nights when you were on duty with Mr. Livancic, what kind of break period would you take to have a sleep? I think you may have already said it was a couple of hours at a time, but perhaps you would confirm. How long did you arrange for each of you to sleep?

utterances.speaker: IVO PRANJKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. Since he was the commander, he would always be on duty, say, from 6.00 until 12.00, that is, from 6.00 in the afternoon until 12.00 at night. Then I would take over at midnight, at 12.00, and stay on until day break, and he would sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Thank you. That concludes my questioning. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaxill. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I have no more questions for the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, we have no questions. Mr. Pranjkovic, thank you for testifying. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, is your next witness Mr. Vidovic, Josip Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: It should be Dragan Calic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, just an observation and a question. We should like, as far as possible, to know the order in which the witnesses appear, because we received a note from Mr. Susak regarding the order of appearance but that order has not been respected, and it is very useful for us, in order to prepare, to be familiar with that order of appearance of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Counsel Susak, I think the Prosecutor is right. We too have the same list, and that's why I mentioned Mr. Vidovic, because he was the next one on the list. Counsel Susak, could you be so kind as to tell us right away the list of your witnesses in the order in which you will call them today and tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I had planned to hear for today Katica Kovac and Ivo Pranjkovic. I didn't know we would finish with these two witnesses so quickly, and I think that the Witness and Victims Unit have caused some confusion. We will hear Dragan Calic, after that Josip Vidovic, and after that Josip Covic, and then for Friday we have Finka Bralo and Anto Bralo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Are all these witnesses here, all the five remaining?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, they are all here. They are here in The Hague, but this is the last witness I have here in the courtroom. For tomorrow, I have Josip Vidovic and Josip Covic. Of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see now that you're following this on your list, but we give a list 24 hours in advance and we have provided a list for today, and I should now like to inform you that Josip Vidovic and Josip Covic will be examined tomorrow, for the benefit of Your Honours and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But could you bring tomorrow three witnesses, just in case?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, I thought of doing that. I always do prepare three witnesses, just in case, and I think Finka Bralo will be here tomorrow, and I would like to have her examined as well tomorrow, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Good morning, Mr. Calic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Will you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Calic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you please tell the Court your full name, date of birth, your occupation, and who you're living with?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Do I need to stand up?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No. You may remain seated.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: My name is Dragan Calic. I'm the father of two children. I have a wife. I'm currently working in an enterprise called Trgovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where do you come from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: From Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you give us your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The 14th of June, 1955.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you. We will start with very specific questions from the outset. Are you familiar with the term "Vjetrenice", "D.D. Vjetrenice, Vitez"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: That used to be my own company that I worked in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Just slow down a little bit, please. Just make a pause now and then. Did Vjetrenice have a warehouse in Santici?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What was the name of that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It was known as warehouse number 3 as part of D.D. Vjetrenice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I was the supervisor of that warehouse, the foreman, warehouse number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When was that warehouse built?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So in 1990 and 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were you then the foreman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The warehouse was moved from Poculica to Santici, and it was newly built in 1990, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that you were the foreman there. Who was employed there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I had two assistant workers and two guards, a total of five.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: All three ethnic groups were represented.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. Croats, Serbs and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you tell us whether that warehouse has a yard and whether it is fenced in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Every warehouse has to have a fence, and this one had one too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is this warehouse next to the road, on the road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It is on the main road linking Vitez to Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I see, the Vitez-Busovaca road. With the help of the usher, I should like to show the witness a sketch before proceeding to other questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit will be marked D26/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Maybe you made a mistake. 26/4?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, D26/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Calic, you have the sketch in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you look at it, please? Look at it under the ELMO, please. Will you take a pen, and move the microphone closer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Is that all right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. Will you show us the road and mark the road with the letter "A"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How many entrance gates are there to this yard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: There are two gates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you describe where they are?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Gate number 1 is the main entrance (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You call it the main entrance, so give it the number 1.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And the second one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The auxiliary entrance number 2 on the side entrance (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did those gates exist in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you tell us the role of gate number 1 and, separately, of gate number 2?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Gate number 1 was used for the entry of goods into the warehouse. It had a small gate that was always open and it was never locked. Gate number 1 was used for the entrance of transport vehicles, and it had an additional small gate which was never locked, and it was used by us, the personnel, and also by the consumers, by the customers. Gate number 2, when a truck enters, it had to go out through that gate because the area was not large and the driver could not turn around, so he would go out through gate number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you draw a line from gate number 1 to number 2, the route taken by trucks? Will you please draw a line showing the route taken by trucks? Just draw a line.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. That's all regarding this sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, on the 11th of February, during the hearing here, 11th of February, 1999, in my opinion made the wrong conclusion, that there was only one gate. It can be found on the transcript, 6.846, during the testimony of witness Zoran Strukar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Are you asking a question? Because you are now making a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is just by way of an introduction. You were not a member of the Trial Chamber at the time. Judge May was the president of the Trial Chamber. The Judge cautioned me at the time that I should tender certain documents through another witness. That advice was welcome, and that witness is this foreman. So I'm saying this by way of introduction. This is of no significance for the Prosecution or for the Defence, because these are photographs taken on the 16th of April, 1993, photographs taken by UNPROFOR. For this reason, I should like to ask the usher to show these photographs to the witness. This was Prosecution Exhibit P245.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: There are some marks on these photographs, something has been written over them, but that is no obstacle for you to show us what is to the right of this tank and whether there is an entrance gate to the Ogrjev warehouse. This photograph was taken on the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is a photograph from '93. Do you recognise the entrance gate to the Ogrjev warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you describe it and mark it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It's not a very good photograph. It's better on the monitor than on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, then, look at it on the monitor and tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Do I need to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, do. Mark it with the number "2."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you put a circle around that gate.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Will you tell us, what is there that is whitish? Why is this white path, and when you take a photograph today, there's no path?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Every gate has to have an access path, and if you can't see it nowadays, it's probably covered over with grass because it's not being used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I see. So it's not being used. Tell us which gate this is. You showed us two on the sketch a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: This is the side entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is it the gate leading from the asphalt road to the yard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it wasn't always used. We called it an auxiliary gate, a side gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could we ask the usher now to show the witness another aerial photograph, also taken in 1993. This was Prosecution Exhibit 247.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Will this exhibit be marked on by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. So will you mark it as D27/4, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first photograph is marked D27/4, and the new one will be marked D28/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Calic, is that the same gate that we saw a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Which gate is this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: This is gate number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you mark it with number "1," please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you explain to Their Honours how one enters the warehouse through this gate? Do you enter it from the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then there is a small 30-metre long path, and then you enter the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How far is the gate from the asphalt part of the road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Thirty metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you draw a line from the asphalt to the gate and put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You see those small pillars there, the smaller and thicker ones?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are the thicker ones along the road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Calic, you see those concrete poles along the roadside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Here, you mean (indicating)?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Are those pillars used for the iron gate, entrance gate? You said you entered through the other side.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, on this side, they were used for the fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And those over there for another purpose? So in order to enter the Ogrjev warehouse, you can't do it straight from the road, but you have to take a 30-metre long dirt road? Very well. On this photograph, will you mark with an arrow the direction from the entrance gate to the guard post? Just a line with an arrow, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. So that's the path you would take. And if you entered through the other gate, what would it look like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: You mean from the other gate?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. Will you draw a line from the other gate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. We're done with that. We have taken photographs of those same gates on the 19th of April this year, so I would like the usher for his assistance to show these photographs to the witness so that we can compare them with the photographs from 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Calic, this is Exhibit D29/4. Will you please look at these photographs and tell us, photograph number 1, what gate does it show?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Gate Number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you mark it with the number "2," and draw an arrow from that gate in the direction of the guard house, which can't really be seen here; just an arrow, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Fine. Now go on to photograph number 3 and see whether it also shows gate number 2.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you put a circle around it, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you put a cross on the actual gate as it opens, the entrance gate.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: You mean the entrance gate next to the road?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is this wooden hut?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It's a toilet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did it exist in '93?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you see it on the previous photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, tell me what photograph number 2 shows. Is the entrance gate shown here too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you mark it, please, with an "X."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is that gate number 1, or number 2?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Number 2, next to the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, in front of that gate, the path no longer exists. Where did that path go before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It went inside the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But before the fence was built, the path was maybe used by the local people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now mark with a "Y" the place where the toilet is. That is next to gate number 1, you said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, gate number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course, gate number 2. Mr. Calic, we've finished with those photographs. I have some more questions for you. You said that you were the foreman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you have any guards there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What was the role of the guards, and what was your role there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Every warehouse had a foreman, and that was what I was. I had two assistant workers and two guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When did the guards start performing their duties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: From 4.00 p.m. until 8.00 a.m. the next day, until 0800 hours the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And when did you come to work in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: If I didn't come at 8.00, then my assistant would come. Anyway, someone had to be there at 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could a guard leave the warehouse before you came to work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: According to all the rules of the company, he should not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So was what his duty?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: His duty was to wait until the assistant or the foreman arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And then he would leave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How did they perform their duties? Were they two per shift?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, they were one per shift. They would be working one night and resting the next night. So they took turns.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Gate number 1 that was next to the asphalt road, was it ever locked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The big one, yes, and the small one, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you misunderstood me. We are talking about two entrances to the warehouse. I'm talking about gate number 1, next to the asphalt road. Was it locked, or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. You mean the big gate? There's a big gate and a smaller gate next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I asked you before to explain whether there were two gates to enter the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, two big ones. But this -- one of the big ones had an additional gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'm talking about the two big ones. We're talking about the gate next to the asphalt road, number 1. Was it locked or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: For security's sake, so that cars couldn't enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where was the key kept?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: In the desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When was it unlocked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: In the morning, when you come to work at 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did this gate have an auxiliary entrance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'm talking about the same gate, next to the asphalt road. How many doors did it have? I'm not talking about the big gate; I'm talking about gate number 1, next to the asphalt road. I'm talking about the gate next to the asphalt road, where the trucks entered, next to the toilet.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It was locked non-stop. It was locked all the time. I was talking about the other gate, the number 1 entrance gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mean gate number 2? Sorry, in that case it's my mistake. So gate number 2 was always locked, and when would be it unlocked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Only when goods were being unloaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where was the key kept to that gate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: In the desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now we're going on to the other gate. How would you enter through that other gate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: You would enter by a kind of side door.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So that gate had an auxiliary entrance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How many doors did that gate have?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It had an auxiliary entrance plus two wings of the big gate. The big one was locked and the small auxiliary one was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: For clarity's sake, I should like to show another photograph with the help of the usher, and then we are through with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Calic, this photograph shows gates number 1 and 2. Will you please tell us which gate is which? Are they the same gates we saw on the '93 photograph, which gate is being shown on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: We call it gate number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: With the auxiliary door. How do you enter this gate? Will you show us with an arrow?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And on the second photograph, and here, how do you enter? Do you enter it straight from the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It's about three metres away from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So will you mark the entrance through the second gate.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Fine. Where is the toilet, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: How shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So we are through with that now. Thank you. You said that this main gate that we marked with a number "1" was locked, but the small side door to it was not locked. Why was that side door not locked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: For the need of communication. People kept coming and going. For a time there was no water inside, so you had to go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And during the night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It wasn't locked during the night either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why not, if there were guards there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: We simply didn't do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The keys were always in the drawer of the desk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When talking about the guards' hut, was it locked, and do you know the layout of that small hut? Could you describe it to us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The guards' hut consisted of two parts. The first part was a kind of living room, and the second part was a kind of office for me. The living room had an entrance door with a glass pane and one window, and my office also had a glass door and a window. Again, neither of these doors were locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were the windows locked from the inside, or from the outside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: From the inside, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was there glass in the windows and the doors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were paned with glass.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: If a person were to be locked in that room, could he leave the hut?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Calic, give us a whole sentence.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Whoever were to be locked inside could leave it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Because it was easy to open the door from the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How high were the windows from the floor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: 1,20 to 1,50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mentioned two rooms in that guards' hut. Was there a door between the two rooms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Of course. There was a connecting door between the two premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they were never locked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mentioned the windows on that hut. How many windows were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: There were three windows to both rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: One faced where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: One faced westwards, the other one eastwards, and the third one southwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you tell us, who were the guards in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The guards were Borko Mijatovic and Aladin Karahodza.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How old was Aladin Karahodza, roughly, and what did he look like? What was his appearance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I think he was between 27 and 30, something like that. Physically, he was rather skinny.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was he healthy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Was he in the guards' hut on the 15th, 16th, and 17th and on; do you know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Well, he took over the shift, and probably he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it his turn to be there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We are now talking about the 15th, so was he on duty on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: He arrived before 16.00 hours and took over his duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Up to what time was he to be there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Until 8.00 a.m. on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who was to come to work on the 16th of April, 1993, you as the foreman or someone else, for that guard to be able to go home?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Well, it was an unwritten rule, whoever arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So he had to wait until 8.00 a.m. the following morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. He could go regardless of who arrived, whether it was the assistant or the foreman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you come to work on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were you supposed to come to work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please give us a complete sentence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I was supposed to come, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why didn't you come to work on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, I didn't come to work because of the gunfire, and also I have a stomach ulcer and I wasn't feeling well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: According to the rules, was the guard allowed to leave his post before the foreman arrived at work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The guard, according to the written rules of the company, was not supposed to leave his post.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Since the yard is fenced in, could you tell us what the fence looks like?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The yard is fenced in with concrete posts and a wire fence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This guard, since he was thin, could he have climbed over the fence even if he had been locked in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Considering the strength of the fence itself, a man like Aladin could have got over the fence. He could have climbed over the wire, and I think that an even heavier man could have done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How tall is that fence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The wire fence is 2,20 metres high.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is there a gap between the ground and the fence or does the fence go right down to the ground?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Between the ground and the fence, there is no gap, because when we put the fence there, then we put sand under it. We filled the gap with sand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I would now like to ask the usher to take this set of photographs, because it will help us to get through the next evidence more quickly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The last photograph is marked D30/4. This is D31/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Calic, you have before you a set of photographs. Would you please look at photograph number 1 and circle the small gate, gate number 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is the small door? Could you circle the small door on that gate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Photograph number 1?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. Photograph number 1, does it show the gate number 1 which we marked on the UNPROFOR photograph which we looked at before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can you see what you called the small door which was never locked on that gate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can you circle it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So this is it. The other entrance door consists of what, where a truck would pass through?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The auxiliary door?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the auxiliary door is where you put a circle, and this was for people to go in. Where would a truck go in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is the gate in front of you, so you have put a circle on the small door. Could you now please indicate what else the gate consists of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Two big doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you mark these two big doors with "X" and "Y", please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now you will look at photograph number 4. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Photograph number 4, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You have problems with your eyesight, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, you have a photograph in front of you. Could you please look at photograph number 4? Do you see the hut there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see a part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you see the window?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is that window glazed and is it on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you please put an "X" on that window?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now could you look at photograph number 5? What window is it? Is that the hut where this man is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, and this is the west window (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where does it face?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: To the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Whose houses are west of that window? Are they Muslim houses or Croatian houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Well, the first house is a Muslim house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. We have finished with this part. Now would you please look at photograph number 6? Is that the guards' hut that we can see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: We can see only a corner of the guards' hut.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But we can see the window? Can we see the window?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How is it that I can see it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I can see it on photograph number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I was asking you about photograph number 7.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the window on photograph number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you please mark it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now we will look at the next page, photograph number 11. Is this the entrance door leading to the office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you mark it with an "X"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is there to the right of the door?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: This is the eastern window.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you mark it with "Y"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: (Witness complies)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now would you look at photograph number 13? What does it represent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: A window.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can we see how this window can be opened and closed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: From the inside of the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: From the inside, can you see the knob or the handle by which the window is opened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We have now completed this part of the questioning. Mr. Calic, you said that you were ill?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you go to the doctor then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I went to the doctor in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On that day or later?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: On that day, the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When did you come back to the warehouse compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the 18th of April. What condition did you find the hut in where your office is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I found the hut in a completely normal state, just as we had left it when we were leaving it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you speak closer to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: On the 18th, I found the hut in the same condition as it was when I left it, so there were no changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you see any shattered windows or doors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, nothing was shattered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was the door locked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, the door wasn't locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Was there a telephone in the guards' hut or in your office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a telephone in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you find it there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I found it there when I came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it in working order or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was in working order, but there was no signal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So it wasn't broken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you find anything else in the hut?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: In the office in the hut, I found, because every guard had a pistol with two rounds of ammunition belonging to the company, I found this in good order, and I also found the book where records were kept of the weapons of the guards and observations made by the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was anything noted down by the guard in that book?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, nothing. There was no change.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So what did you find on the desk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Well, in the drawer I found a pistol and two rounds of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was Aladin Karahodza issued with that pistol and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had been issued with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would now like to show a video. If there is not to be a break, I would like to finish with this witness today, Mr. President, if it is possible. I think I will be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, Counsel Susak, but we need a break, a 15-minute break, because of the interpreters. Do you want now to have a break and then we resume in 15 minutes, or do you want to show, first of all, this videotape?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could see the videotape before the break, because that will leave less for after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: It is Exhibit D12/4. D12/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Then you will tell us whether this is the gate.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: This is gate number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Number 1, which doesn't give onto the asphalt road right away?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's about 30 metres away from the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So this is the wire fence. Is the wire strong enough for someone to climb over it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's like a kind of ladder, so you can climb it like a ladder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is this the guards' hut?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Has anything been added to it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you see the changes now on this video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can you describe what has been added on to it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't see it. You have to go forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, the video is going its own way. So this is the gate; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. So first you have to leave the asphalt road, and then you come to the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is the small door?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Whose houses are these?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: This house which is destroyed is a Muslim house. I don't know about the others because I am not a native of Santici. I don't live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So we can see that you can't go straight from the road through the gate, and this is the guards' hut. This is how you enter from the outside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is the small door?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: These are the windows on the guards' hut. Can you see them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the western and the southern window.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is the west window?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is the door?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, the auxiliary gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So this is the door which opens and closes and is never locked. Could you speed up this video, please? I don't think we need to linger.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can you see, this fence goes right down to the ground, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is where I would like the video to be stopped for a minute, where we can see the man climbing over the fence. Could you go back a little, please? Would you stop now, and can we look at it at normal speed now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So is it possible to climb over this fence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's eight times six.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This man is a little heavier than Aladin Karahodza?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And it would be easier if he stayed closer to the concrete post?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: To the east of this house are Muslim houses, so Karahodza could always have jumped out through the window and climbed over the fence. You can speed it up now, please. Now could you stop, please? And this is still the gate, gate number 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is the traffic going along the road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, along the Vitez-Busovaca road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You say these houses are Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you describe this hut? Do you know whether anything has been added to it and how?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the cease-fire, it was extended. Can you see the change?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's here; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: To the right of the door?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I look at it, it's on my right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But the door was always there, and so was this window; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why, as other witnesses have said, did not Aladin Karahodza leave the company throughout the day on the 16th, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Well, on that day, in my personal opinion, I think there was a lot of gunfire on that day and that's why he couldn't leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So he couldn't leave because of the gunfire. If he had wanted to, could he have gone out through the door of the guards' hut and out through the main gate?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes, he could have, because neither the gate nor the door of the office was locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could he have opened the window in the guards' hut which are closed from the inside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Since he was most probably inside, of course, he could have opened the windows because the handles are on the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know that the most intense fighting on the 16th of April, 1993, was along the road where the warehouse is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't hear you. I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I said was the most intense fighting along the road where the warehouse is located? I'm referring to the 16th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were some Muslims killed to the left and to the right of Ogrjev, whose houses are located in the vicinity of Ogrjev?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there the next day, I heard something about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So I'm asking you what you heard. You heard that there had been gunfire all day; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is the window opening which opens from the inside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: This is an electric heater.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you ever lock your room in that guards' hut?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Oh, it wasn't usual, it wasn't our habit, because there was a safe where I kept my documents to which I alone had the key.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: This is the iron fence. I think that this is enough, Mr. President. I would now like to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We'll take a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Calic, so you worked in that compound. Will you please explain if the small door on that gate marked "1" was locked or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The small door at gate number 1 was never locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was there a key to that door?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: There was a key to the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And where was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It was with other keys in the desk in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: After April 16th, you came to the guards' hut, did you find the keys there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I found the keys in the desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you find the keys to all doors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: They were all on one, what should I call it, they were all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they were all hanging on one and the same ring. How do you explain, then, that some witnesses saw Aladin Karahodza run across the yard on the 16th of April, '93, in the afternoon, across the yard to gate number 2, towards the asphalt road where the UNPROFOR tank was? How do you explain that he ran in that direction rather than to the main gate, which is gate number 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Pardon me if I interrupt, but I just doubt the validity of the question. The witness has already clearly stated he was nowhere near the building on the 16th of April, so he is being asked essentially not even to comment on what may have been said to him but to speculate why a man ran in one direction and not another, and he cannot speak to that, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's a good objection. Counsel Susak, can you move on to another question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I do not agree with this objection, but then I will move on to another question. Mr. Calic knows the area, the houses, and the deployment of Muslims who were armed, and Croats as well. So that is perhaps why Aladin Karahodza chose the road to gate number 2 rather than gate number 1. However, I will leave that question aside and ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: If you go from the guard hut to gate number 1 as against moving from that hut to number 2, is there a better shelter when one moves towards gate number 2 than towards gate number 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Since the office had an extension, a roofed part where the goods were unloaded, it was better sheltered from any fire, from any bullets, than gate number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it a problem for Aladin Karahodza to climb over the wire fence at gate 2?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The wire fence is the same all around. The whole compound was encircled by the same wire fence, so he could have climbed it at any place.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was there some area -- was there some free room between the wire fence and the ground? Could one get under the wire fence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: There was absolutely no room for a cat to get through, let alone a man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should like to round off my questions. On the first videotape there is no gate number 2. I should like to finish my questions with showing briefly tape number 2, and it is about the warehouse of Ogrjev. I'm proposing to do this because it was not clear at the outset whether there were one or two gates to the Ogrjev warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: But is it necessary? I mean, is it disputed that there were two entrances?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No, not at all. And certainly, if we are looking to 1993, the witness has clearly stated there were two sets of large gates which were in use for vehicular access. We are quite happy to agree with that as being as read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. It is not disputed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, my learned friend from the Prosecution, for accepting this and thus saving time for all of us. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one more thing. I should like to tender all these documents into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. They are admitted into evidence. Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, other Defence counsel have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I have a few, Your Honours, and I can assure you, very briefly, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Sir, if I can just ask you a number of questions, my name is Michael Blaxill, I'm one of the Prosecutors in this case. I think we have just confirmed that you had two sets of large gates which were used in 1993 for vehicles to gain access and to exit from the Ogrjev premises; that is correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes. In 1993, there were two gates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When they were not being used for vehicular access, I believe you said that those gates, the big ones were locked, but the small personnel gate was kept open at all times; that is also correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It is. The small gate was always kept open for communication, for getting into and getting out of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And as to the wire fence around the premises, has that been changed in any way since 1993? Has the wire been renewed? If it's renewed, is it the same style of wire that there was there in 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, it has not been changed at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Just to confirm, you were at work, were you, on the 15th of April of '93?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: You did not go near the Ogrjev premises at all on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: And the next time you went to work was the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: No, the 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: The 18th of April? Thank you, sir. I would like, if I may, you to look at the exhibit we've marked, I think it's 27/4. It's the picture with an UNPROFOR tank on the street. Do you have that one there, sir? I'm going to ask you one question. It may be a little unclear on that photograph, though I do have a clearer colour one if we need to refer to it. Sir, if you look at the gate, the entrance gates that are seen on that photograph, to my eye it looks as though there is a bit of a gap between the bottom of the gate and the ground. Is that so? Was there a gap there in 1993, below those gates?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The gate itself, the gate itself is attached to posts which keep it fixed. Of course there must have been some 5-centimetre gap simply so as to be able to open the gate, because one cannot really have the gate reaching down to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: So how deep was that gap, do you think?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The gate itself, you mean? I believe about five metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: No, sorry, I meant the gap between the bottom of the gate and the ground.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Five centimetres, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: One final thing, sir. Just to confirm, I believe you've already stated it, the gate, the small personnel gate that you did not lock was actually capable of being locked; that is correct? And there was a key for it; yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: There was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I'd like to confer for just one moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: One final point, if I may. Your guards did have, did they not, a pistol and some ammunition on the premises of the guardhouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: When you returned to work on the 18th of April, did you, in fact, have cause to check whether the gun was still there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: The gun was there where one always left it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Where was it -- I'm sorry. Did you want to finish something?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: Together with ammunition, two rounds of bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Where was that, in fact, kept?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN CALIC
utterances.text: It was kept -- I mean the pistol and ammunition were kept in the desk and the table that we also used for lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: That actually concludes my questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaxill. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We have no questions, so therefore, Mr. Calic, thank you for giving evidence in court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Susak, I gather you have no witness available?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: No, I do not have any more witnesses, because I really could not anticipate when we would be finished with this witness. So we shall continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. We will adjourn now until tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 12.55 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 24th day of June, 1999, at 9.00 a.m.
